work_or_witness: Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura · FAQ v1.0 introduction, lines 19-21
definition: The unstable equilibrium/dichotomy central to Arcanum's world, with technology rising and magic declining in the official FAQ's setting description.
cultural_caution: A source-specific setting tension, not a universal real-world model of science, religion, or industrial development.

supports: magic/technology equilibrium, industrialization, and story premise

definition: The system by which the player can create a character or choose one of many pre-fabricated characters.
cultural_caution: A player-avatar system; no selectable/pre-fabricated protagonist is a stable character node in this pass.

definition: NPCs who may receive commands such as walk, attack, stay close, spread out, and back off; followers can be addressed by name.
cultural_caution: Optional party-control framework, not proof that every NPC or named follower joins a particular player campaign.

supports: follower command system and Virgil example

definition: A player-character state that may be affected by dialogue choices in the manual's Virgil tutorial encounter.
cultural_caution: A player-variable mechanic, not a moral category applied to a fixed NPC without evidence.

definition: The opening guided location containing debris, hostile wolves, a cave, Virgil, and Charles Brehgo's spirit encounter.
cultural_caution: A place/tutorial context, not a character endpoint or exhaustive account of the crash event.

supports: Crash Site, debris, wolves, cave, Virgil, and Charles Brehgo context

definition: An optional combat mode displaying action points; the manual contrasts it with real-time combat.
cultural_caution: A player-selectable rules mode, not a fixed in-fiction fighting style or a claim about campaign outcome.

supports: turn-based mode, action points, and real-time-combat contrast

definition: Systems governing item usefulness and the capacity to make new items, illustrated through the tutorial's technological schematics.
cultural_caution: Customizable player capability systems, not a stable character vocation or a complete technology taxonomy.

supports: skills, schematics, technological schematics, and item-making context

definition: A diegetic manual section that discusses elves, orcs, humans, dwarves, ogres, gnomes, and halflings as thinking creatures/peoples.
cultural_caution: The manual's in-world racial classification contains fictional essentialism, prejudice, and colonial-science-style framing. It is neither endorsed nor mapped to real peoples, races, or ethnicities.

supports: Races section, listed peoples, and diegetic naturalist framing

definition: The source-native term used in the manual's fictional racial treatise for the basis of technological development.
cultural_caution: A diegetic philosophical/scientific expression from a prejudicial fictional text; not equated with real scientific practice or a universal technology system.

supports: Natural Law and technology wording in manual's human-race passage

definition: A distinct mode in which turn-based combat is unavailable and some spells do not work on playing characters because the game does not control player reactions.
cultural_caution: A separate play mode, not evidence for single-player story canon or player-character identity.

supports: multiplayer restriction and player-character spell-immunity rationale
